ranking.note: Raised to P1: responsibly disclosed flaw where release verification counts revoked/expired keys, i.e. users can be told a release is verified when it is not — the most consequential correctness problem in this list.
Raised to P2: supported-platform failure of the new bitcoin wrapper on Windows (exit codes lost, functional tests disabled) and prerequisite for #36190.
Raised to P2 for consistency with #36105: the wrapper is unusable on distributions with custom bindir/libexecdir (Arch), a packaging-level breakage felt by real users.
Placed lower than its score position: a pure developer/debugging convenience, ranked below tool bugs that break existing workflows (seed generation, completions drift, datadir).
Lowered to P4: refactoring aid with no stated user payoff, author himself prefers abandoning it in favour of manual rewrites.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36190 only tests behaviour introduced by #36105 and depends on it; review #36105 first, then #36190 as its regression guard.
#19460 sits on top of the multiprocess branch (#10102/#29409) and is the base for #19461; its value is conditional on that branch progressing.
#35903 may already be unreachable after #35958 (raised in its own thread) — confirm before spending review time; if so it is redundant rather than a bug fix.

#27409 builds on merged #27302 and overlaps in spirit with the wrapper path fixes (#36106): both concern CLI tools resolving the wrong locations; worth reviewing with a consistent story on path/datadir resolution.
#35788 (bitcoin-util evalscript) and #35814 (autogenerated completions) are both new tool surface added to the same CLI family; no conflict, but they compete for the same reviewer attention pool.
result.notes: The list is dominated by contrib/developer-script work; only #36293 has a security consequence for downstream users, and the two wrapper fixes are the only supported-platform breakages, so the P1/P2 tier is deliberately small and the long P3 tail reflects genuinely deferrable tooling.
